name: OAuth2 session-bridge
purpose: The single point where a resolved provider identity crosses into the project's session vocabulary. Owns the derivation of the reduced Principal shape, the issue-and-verify contract for the project session cookie, the storage of the provider tokens (access, id, refresh) associated with the session, and the invalidation on sign-out. Every downstream code path that reads `request.auth` reads what this bridge lifted; nothing downstream sees the provider's raw claim shape.
responsibilities: Derive `principalId` as a stable string composed from `{provider.id, sub}` (OIDC) or `{provider.id, userinfo.id}` (oauth2-only); refuse an identity with a missing subject with `OAUTH2_SUBJECT_MISSING` (AC-10106-1, AC-10109-1).

Populate the reduced Principal with `principalId`, `provider`, optional `email`, empty `roles[]`, empty `organisationIds[]`; expose a project-authored `enrichPrincipal(principal) -> principal` hook if the config declares one; refuse to expose provider tokens on the Principal (AC-10106-1, AC-10106-3).

Issue an opaque-handle session cookie: mint a cryptographically random handle, store the session record `{ handle, principal, providerId, accessToken, idToken, refreshToken?, issuedAt, expiresAt }` in the session-record store, and emit `Set-Cookie` with `HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Lax` (AC-10101-3, AC-10106-1).

Verify a presented handle at the middleware boundary: lookup, expiry check, tampered-value refusal, populate `request.auth` on success, refuse otherwise; do not renew a tampered cookie (AC-10106-1, AC-10106-2).
Invalidate on sign-out: delete the session record, clear the associated refresh-token chain, emit the cookie-clear header (AC-10108-1).

Delegate the session-record store to a project-authored implementation (in-memory for the reference wiring; SQLite for `persistence-data-sqlite`-composed projects; D1 for `persistence-data-d1`-composed projects); do not embed a store implementation (REQ-006).
internalStructure: One factory function producing an issue/verify/invalidate closure over an injected `sessionRecordStore`, an injected `refreshTokenStore` (shared with the flow controller), an injected `randomBytes` port for handle minting, an injected clock, and an injected `enrichPrincipal` hook (or a no-op default). The session-record shape is a plain object; the store's on-disk shape is the project's concern.

interfaces.name: sessionRecordStore
interfaces.description: Project-supplied store exposing `put(handle, record)`, `get(handle) -> record | absent`, `delete(handle)`, and `purgeExpired(now)`. In-memory is the reference default; a persistence-data-sqlite-composed project points this at a table.

interfaces.name: refreshTokenStore
interfaces.description: Shared with the flow controller: exposes `put(handle, refreshToken)`, `clearChain(chainRoot)`.

interfaces.name: randomBytes
interfaces.description: Cryptographic random-byte source used to mint session handles; a 128-bit-or-more entropy budget is expected.

interfaces.name: clock
interfaces.description: Injected time source; the same clock the flow controller uses.

interfaces.name: enrichPrincipal
interfaces.description: Optional project-authored hook called on the reduced Principal to add `roles` and `organisationIds` from project-side sources. A no-op default is applied when the config does not declare one.

dependencies.name: OAuth2 flow controller
dependencies.description: The bridge is invoked by the controller at the end of a successful callback; the bridge does not initiate flows.

tradeoffs: Deriving `principalId` from `{provider.id, subject}` prevents accidental cross-provider identity merging; the trade is that a project that wants such merging must author an explicit identity-merge policy in its enrichPrincipal hook. Storing provider tokens on the server-side session record rather than the browser cookie carries a small per-session storage cost and buys the project one code path for revocation on sign-out and refresh-token reuse; the tokens never appear in a place the browser can leak them. Exposing an `enrichPrincipal` hook without prescribing a role-source lets a project reach for its own claim-mapping vocabulary without the blueprint committing to one.
